profiles.meeting_scenario: A pediatric proton therapy planning meeting at a tertiary cancer center is being held to prepare a cross-institutional implementation package for a standardized passively scattered proton craniospinal irradiation (CSI) planning methodology. The center plans to share a reproducible planning workflow with two partner hospitals that are starting comparative dosimetric studies. The immediate agenda is to decide what materials will be prepared over the next three weeks: the planning template, the written technique notes, the sample case set, and the summary outputs that partner sites will use to judge whether they reproduced the method correctly. The expected outcome is a concrete work plan assigning who will assemble the reference plans, what counts as the standard organ-dose summary, which representative cases will be included, and when the package will be ready for internal review.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.expertise: Craniospinal irradiation target delineation, pediatric proton therapy protocols, cross-institutional clinical standardization
members.background: Dr. Park leads the pediatric CNS disease site group and helped adapt the institution's proton CSI approach for younger and older pediatric anatomies; she routinely focuses on making planning methods clinically interpretable and transferable across centers.
members.private_state: She wants the package to be simple enough that partner physicians will actually use it, and she is worried that too much technical detail or too many exceptions will make the methodology look non-portable.
hidden_assumptions: A 'representative case' set should include one younger child and one older child because the key clinical distinction is the age-specific target volume definition.
An 'internal review' of the package means a physician-level review for clinical face validity before anything is circulated externally.
If the package reports organ doses, sites will naturally understand that the important numbers are the summary table values used in comparative papers, not full planning-system exports.
When the team says the method should be 'reproducible,' that mainly means another center can follow the same clinical field arrangement logic and obtain similar organ sparing patterns.

members.name: Michael Tran
members.expertise: Passively scattered proton field design, compensator and aperture workflow, treatment planning system documentation, dosimetric QA
members.background: Michael has built most of the center's passively scattered CSI plans over the last six years and is often responsible for translating physician intent into executable planning instructions and benchmark datasets for outside collaborators.
members.private_state: He wants the package to be precise enough that outside sites cannot claim they followed the method while making different technical choices, and he is concerned about last-minute physician edits disrupting the build schedule.
hidden_assumptions: A 'representative case' set should include one straightforward anatomy and one technically difficult anatomy to capture setup and compensator edge conditions, regardless of age grouping.
An 'internal review' means a physics/dosimetry reproducibility check after all plan objects, DVHs, and parameter sheets are assembled.
If the package reports organ doses, outside sites will need exported DVH data and exact structure naming/mapping to reproduce the same summaries.
When the team says the method should be 'reproducible,' that mainly means another planner can recreate the same beam parameters, junction handling, and dosimetric outputs with minimal interpretation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include 'two representative patients' in the implementation package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means one patient from each of the two age-specific target volume groups used in the methodology.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means one technically simple case and one technically challenging case that illustrate planning execution extremes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both uses of 'representative' sound professionally standard and reasonable in this context, so each hears the phrase as confirming their own obvious sampling logic without feeling any need to unpack it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to send a 'standard organ-dose summary' for partner institutions to compare against.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a concise manuscript-style table of minimum, maximum, and mean dose values for the ten named organs, as percentages of prescribed dose, because that is the clinically digestible benchmark.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects exported cumulative DVH files plus structure labels and calculation notes, from which the partner sites can derive whatever summary statistics they need.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In clinical planning discussions, 'organ-dose summary' can naturally refer either to a table or to the underlying dosimetric package, and both formats are commonly treated as serving the same purpose of comparison.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the package should be 'ready for internal review' by the end of next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the package is review-ready once the written technique notes, selected cases, and headline dosimetric results are assembled well enough for clinicians to confirm the method's clinical framing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes it is review-ready only when the actual planning artifacts are complete enough for dosimetry/physics to rerun checks and verify reproducibility without missing plan objects.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to using 'internal review' as a shared milestone, but in their local workflow different disciplines apply different sufficiency standards to that same phrase, and the meeting context makes it sound like ordinary scheduling shorthand.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using 'the 18-patient cohort' as the basis for the package examples and summary numbers.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the original study cohort exactly as analyzed for publication, with the age-based subgrouping and the already-vetted summary outputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the internally archived set of 18 planning cases derived from that effort, including later replans and updated structure labels that replaced some original exported files.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both parties routinely call both datasets 'the 18-patient cohort,' and because the internal archive descended from the publication project, the reference feels identical unless someone explicitly distinguishes publication-final data from current planning files.

turns.inner_thought: We need a package the partner physicians can absorb quickly, not a giant technical dump. If we can get the written notes, the selected example cases, and the headline dose results together by end of next week, that's ready for internal review from my standpoint. I want the clinicians to look at it first and make sure the framing is portable before the team buries it in planning details.

turns.inner_thought: End of next week is tight but doable if the build is anchored to the archived planning set. Using the 18-patient cohort gives me the plan objects, later replans, and the updated structure labels I trust, and it covers enough variation that outside sites can't say the method only works in cherry-picked anatomy. Internal review means physics and dosimetry can actually rerun the checks, so I need complete materials, not just a narrative shell.

If we keep it to two representative patients and a short explanation of the age-specific target volume approach, the package stays understandable and portable.
turns.utterance: Great. For the external package, I think we should include two representative patients along with a concise write-up of the age-specific target volume approach, so outside physicians can orient themselves quickly.

turns.inner_thought: He seems aligned. We also need a simple comparison output. I'll export the DVHs, the structure mapping, and notes from the 18-patient cohort archive. That way the package has the underlying dosimetry rather than just a polished top-line table.

turns.inner_thought: That's fine as background material, but for the actual summary page I want the familiar compact values from the paper outputs. turns.utterance: Perfect. For the summary page itself, I mainly want the same minimum, maximum, and mean values as percentages of prescription, since that's what collaborators will recognize immediately.

turns.inner_thought: Once I have the exports organized and the parameter sheets cleaned up, internal review should just be physics checking that the files are complete and reproducible in one pass. turns.inner_thought: I need to make sure the clinicians see it first for clinical face validity. I do not want the message diluted by too much technical apparatus before we've confirmed the clinical presentation works.
